A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same LLMVS research work, with complete main text, references, and Appendices A–C. Text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, zero-shot transfer results, and qualitative examples in Sections 4 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments in Tables 1–6 and A1–A3, alongside qualitative results in Figures 5 and B1.

M1.justification: The caption generation, local scoring, query/answer embedding extraction, global self-attention aggregation, and MSE objective remain unchanged. Figure 4’s label corrections do not alter the architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SumMe and TVSum and conduct zero-shot testing on MR.HiSum. The qualitative figures retain the same four video examples; no dataset, task, or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1 and 6, including the visual and multimodal baselines and the LLM comparison. The comparison configurations in the analysis tables are also retained.

E3.justification: Both versions report the same five-fold evaluation protocol, Kendall’s tau and Spearman’s rho metrics, summary construction procedure, training settings, and 50-video MR.HiSum evaluation. The revised qualitative curves are not accompanied by a reported protocol change.

E4.justification: The qualitative comparisons with human scores contain revised prediction traces in Figure 5(a–b) and Figure B1(b), changing the evidence displayed for existing case studies. The cases, analytical questions, ablations, sensitivity studies, and zero-shot analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting remains unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the proposed method.

E6.justification: The displayed LLMVS prediction trajectories change in the three TVSum examples in Figures 5 and B1(b); the SumMe binary-summary example is retained. All values in Tables 1–6 and A1–A3 remain unchanged. The PDFs do not explain the revised trajectories or establish a performance improvement.

T1.justification: The problem definition, mathematical model specification, and MSE loss in Equations 1–6 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about language-based summarization, local/global context, output embeddings, and state-of-the-art benchmark performance.

C2.justification: The explanations of contextual embeddings, individual user preferences, generalization, and action-oriented content remain unchanged. The qualitative discussions are retained despite the revised prediction curves, and no substantive limitation is added.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 retains the same model identifiers, hyperparameters, optimizer, 200-epoch budget, five A100 GPUs, and approximate training time. Appendix C’s full prompts and other implementation disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the research positioning throughout the paper, and all 60 references are unchanged.

P1.justification: Figure 4 corrects 'Rotray Positional Encodings' to 'Rotary Positional Encodings' and adjusts label spacing. The arXiv version/date stamp changes, while the prose, headings, section order, and appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 5 and B1 are redrawn with heavier curves and adjusted highlighting, and Figure 4 receives label corrections. These are localized visual revisions; figure placement, captions, examples, and table layouts remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The corrected diagram label and more legible curves provide modest presentation benefits. However, v2 replaces the TVSum prediction traces in Figures 5 and B1(b) without explaining whether they reflect corrected outputs, different runs, or altered processing. With methods and tabulated results unchanged, the PDFs do not establish whether the revised qualitative evidence improves accuracy, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
